commits.edited_message:
rar5: correct extra-field length checks

Two corrections to RAR5 extra-field parsing:

 - In process_head_file_extra(), reject an extra-field size that
   exceeds the remaining extra-field data before subtracting it, so
   the running counter can't underflow.

 - In parse_file_extra_redir(), the link target is copied into a
   MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES buffer, but its length was rejected once it grew
   past MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS.  Compare against the buffer's byte capacity
   instead, so valid long link targets are no longer refused.

(cherry picked from commit 36a093b7e475f9260d1eddceca7985f7824ffee6)

rar5: Adjust read_var/read_var_sized return values

USE ARCHIVE_OK, ARCHIVE_EOF, and ARCHIVE_FATAL for improved error
handling. Integer overflows must not be considered "end of file".

Handle different error message on 32 bit systems in tests.

While here, size the redirect target buffer to MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS so it
matches the enforced filename character limit instead of over-reserving
stack.

Signed-off-by: Tobias Stoeckmann <tobias@stoeckmann.org>
(cherry picked from commit 07599ddf8d50830a375b5a3f927c4020fcb4036d)

coupling:
The defect is a stack-buffer overflow of target_utf8_buf in parse_file_extra_redir() (archive_read_support_format_rar5.c), triggered by the memcpy(target_utf8_buf, p, target_size). Its reachability is split across the two edited commits, and each diff is individually consistent and benign:

- Commit 07076df (earlier) only CHANGES THE LENGTH CHECK from `target_size > MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS - 1` to `target_size > MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES - 1`. At that point in history the destination buffer is still declared `char target_utf8_buf[MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES]` (8192 bytes), so the widened limit exactly matches the buffer capacity -- the diff reads as a correct relaxation that stops rejecting valid long link targets, and copies of up to 8191 bytes still fit.

- Commit e8a2270 (later) only CHANGES THE BUFFER declaration from `MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES` (8192) to `MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS` (2048). Read on its own, sizing a 'utf8 name' buffer to the filename character limit looks like a correct, stack-saving tidy-up; the length-check line is not part of this diff, and the character limit (MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS) is the constant the check historically used, so the change appears to preserve the buffer>=limit invariant.

Neither commit is wrong in isolation: reverting either one restores a matching (limit, buffer) pair and the overflow disappears (verified: reverting only the check -> clean ARCHIVE_FATAL rejection; reverting only the buffer -> 4000-byte target fits the 8192-byte buffer, clean). The bug exists only because 07076df widened the accepted length on the assumption the buffer stayed MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES, while e8a2270 shrank the buffer on the assumption the limit stayed MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS. A correct fix must reconcile BOTH commits (recognise that the length check and the buffer size now reference different constants) -- fixing either single diff in isolation leaves a (limit, buffer) pair that one reviewer would consider internally correct, which is why no per-commit review catches it. MAX_NAME_IN_BYTES is defined as 4 * MAX_NAME_IN_CHARS, so the composed window admits targets up to 8191 bytes into a 2048-byte stack buffer.
